summary: Customer wants to investigate whether optical spectroscopy can track protein concentration in a dairy whey stream ahead of a concentration stage, using laboratory results as reference, and asks for a first measurement concept that copes with the stream turning more turbid instead of assuming it always stays clear.

facts_stated.text: The application is a dairy process.
The stream is whey and is relatively clear at the point of interest.
The measurement point is before a concentration stage.
The measurement interest is protein concentration.
The stream composition/state changes and the measurement must follow it.
Laboratory results are to be the reference.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: with laboratory results used as the reference

facts_stated.text: The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions.

facts_stated.text: The concept must handle the change in clarity rather than assuming the liquid always remains clear.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: handles this change rather than assuming the liquid always remains clear

targets.variable: protein concentration in the whey stream
targets.enquiry_quote: track protein concentration as the stream changes

optical_regime.enquiry_quote: The stream can become more turbid under some operating conditions.

aqueous.enquiry_quote: Our dairy process includes a relatively clear whey stream

customer_premises.claim: Laboratory results are assumed to be an adequate and comparable reference for the in-line measurement.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: with laboratory results used as the reference

customer_premises.claim: A first measurement concept is requested before the deciding facts (target range, matrix, interferences, installation, accuracy) are known.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: We need a first measurement concept

customer_premises.claim: Spectroscopy is assumed to be able to track protein concentration in this stream; feasibility is to be investigated rather than proven.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: whether spectroscopy can track protein concentration

unknowns: which protein species or fraction is meant (total protein vs. specific whey protein) and whether the laboratory reference measures the same quantity
protein concentration range and the magnitude of the changes to be tracked
required accuracy/precision, detection limit and response time
magnitude, frequency and cause of the turbidity change, and whether particulates, fat droplets or air are involved
other matrix components and interferences (fat, lactose, minerals, cleaning chemicals)
temperature and pressure of the stream at the measurement point
installation point, probe or flow-cell geometry, path length and distance between instrument and stream
cleaning (CIP) and fouling behaviour, and applicable sanitary/hygiene standards
details of the laboratory reference method and sampling procedure
flow rate/velocity and whether the measurement must be continuous or intermittent
spectral region or measurement technique considered
